# Desalination
### Thirsty? How 'bout a cool, refreshing cup of seawater?

No, don't take us literally! Humans cannot drink saline water. But, saline water can be made into **fresh water**, which is the purpose of this portable, inflatable solar still (it even wraps up into a tiny package). The process is called desalination, and it is being used more and more around the world to provide people with needed fresh water. Most of the United States has, or can gain access to, ample supplies of fresh water for drinking purposes. But, fresh water can be in short supply in many parts of the Nation and world. And, as the population continues to grow, shortages of fresh water will occur more often, if only in certain locations. In some areas, **salt water** (from the **ocean**, for instance) is being turned into fresh water for drinking.
The "simple" hurdle that must be overcome to turn seawater into fresh water is to remove the dissolved salt in seawater. That may seem as easy as just boiling some seawater in a pan, capturing the steam, and condensing it back into water (distillation). Other methods are available, but these current technological processes must be done on a large scale to be useful to large populations, and the current processes are expensive, energy-intensive, and involve large-scale facilities.

# Desalination
### What makes water saline?
What do we mean by "saline water?" Water that is saline contains significant amounts (referred to as "concentrations") of dissolved salts. In this case, the concentration is the amount (by weight) of salt in water, as expressed in "parts per million" (ppm). If water has a concentration of 10,000 ppm of dissolved salts, then one percent of the weight of the water comes from dissolved salts.
Here are our parameters for saline water:
*   Fresh water - Less than 1,000 ppm  
*   Slightly saline water - From 1,000 ppm to 3,000 ppm  
*   Moderately saline water - From 3,000 ppm to 10,000 ppm  
*   Highly saline water - From 10,000 ppm to 35,000 ppm
For context, ocean water contains about 35,000 ppm of salt.

# Desalination
### The worldwide need for freshwater
The scarcity of fresh water resources and the need for additional water supplies is already critical in many arid regions of the world and will be increasingly important in the future. Many arid areas simply do not have fresh water resources in the form of surface water such as rivers and lakes. They may have only limited **underground water resources****(****groundwater****)**, some that are becoming more brackish as extraction of water from the aquifers continues. Solar desalination - evaporation - is used by nature to produce **rain**, which is the main source of fresh water on earth.
According to the International Desalination Association, globally, more than 300 million people receive their water from de-salination plants. The largest desalination plant in North America, the Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant, can be found near San Diego, California. It produces 50 million gallons a day of fresh water for 110,000 customers in San Diego County where approximately 3.3 million people live.It costs about twice as much as other water sources. At this moment there exists 11 desalination plants in California and 10 more plants have been proposed. The largest desalination plant in the world, Jebel Ali Power Plant and Water Desalination, is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and produces over 588 million gallons of potable water a day.
In 2015, in some States in the U.S., public supply water sources include desalinated seawater or brackish groundwater that has been treated to reduce dissolved solids. A combined total of 7.21 million gallons per day of saline surface water withdrawals for public supply use were reported for the U.S. Virgin Islands, Texas, Florida, and Massachusetts. A combined total of 263 million gallons per day of saline groundwater withdrawals for public-supply use were identified for Florida, California, Texas, Virginia, Kansas, and Utah. (Deiter et al., 2018).

# Desalination
### Another method: Reverse osmosis
Another way saline water is desalinized is by the "reverse osmosis" procedure. In most simplistic terms, water, containing dissolved salt molecules, is forced through a semi-permeable membrane (essentially a filter), in which the larger salt molecules do not get through the membrane holes but the smaller water molecules do.
Reverse osmosis is an effective means to desalinate saline water, but it is more expensive than other methods. As prices come down in the future the use of reverse osmosis plants to desalinate large amounts of saline water should become more common.

# Desalination
### Uses for desalinated water
When we think of desalination we tend to focus on having fresh water to drink but it is important to note that desalinated seawater is not only produced for domestic/municipal use. Desalination provides fresh water for agricultural irrigation and is often used for processes that require extremely good water quality like that used in boilers to avoid scale buildup. Other examples include the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, semi-conductors, and hard disk drives.

# Desalination
### Desalination is not modern science
Distillation desalination is one of mankind's earliest forms of water treatment, and it is still a popular treatment solution throughout the world today. In ancient times, many civilizations used this process on their ships to convert sea water into drinking water. Today, desalination plants are used to convert sea water to drinking water on ships and in many arid regions of the world, and to treat water in other areas that is fouled by natural and unnatural contaminants. Distillation is perhaps the one water treatment technology that most completely reduces the widest range of drinking water contaminants.
In nature, this basic process is responsible for the**water (hydrologic) cycle**. The sun supplies energy that causes water to evaporate from surface sources such as lakes, oceans, and streams. The **water vapor** eventually comes in contact with cooler air, where it re-condenses to form dew or rain. This process can be imitated artificially and more rapidly than in nature, using alternative sources of heating and cooling.

### Why don't we see more desalination plants if freshwater is so scarce?
The primary reason we don't see more desalination plants is due to the cost to operate these plants. Salt dissolves easily in water and it requires a lot of energy to break the chemical bonds. Energy consumption hikes up the cost to run a plant and the cost of the technology to desalinate the water also holds a hefty price tag.
Sometimes environmental protection is a factor that can keep desalination plants from being built. In 2022, after a 20-year plan to build a desalination plant at Huntington Beach in California, the California Coastal Commission declined the bid to build the plant due to concerns about higher water rates, marine life loss, and impacts to poor households already living near industrial areas. Residents in the area did not like that the plant would have taken 100 million daily gallons of seawater, desalted half of it, and discharged the other half back as saltier brine.

Ras Al Khair in Saudi Arabia currently holds the World’s Largest Desalination Plant title, producing close to three million cubic meters of fresh water daily. Riyadh and several nearby cities draw drinking water directly from this one site.
Freshwater shortage sits near the top of the world’s problems right now. Growing populations, expanding industries, and shrinking natural water sources have pushed one country after another toward seawater desalination.
A desalination plant strips salt, minerals, and other impurities out of seawater until it is safe to drink, farm with, or run through a factory. The World’s Largest Desalination Plant rankings show how far this technology has come.

## Which Countries Operate the World’s Largest Desalination Plant Facilities?
Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and India host most of the sites on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list. Each country deals with the same problem: limited freshwater and dense coastal populations.
**A few names show up again and again on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant ranking:**
*   Ras Al Khair and Shuaiba, both in Saudi Arabia  
*   Jebel Ali and Taweelah, in the United Arab Emirates  
*   Sorek, in Israel  
*   Nemmeli, in India
None of these sites operates in isolation. Water from each one feeds straight into municipal supply lines, refineries, power plants, and farmland across the region.

## How Do These Facilities Turn Seawater Into Freshwater?
Reverse Osmosis is the workhorse behind most facilities on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list, though Multi-Stage Flash and Multi-Effect Distillation still show up at several sites. It forces seawater through fine membranes that trap salt and other particles, letting only clean water pass through.
Thermal plants heat seawater until it evaporates, then collect the vapor as pure water. Quite a few large sites run both methods side by side.
Around 300 million people worldwide now rely, one way or another, on water from a World’s Largest Desalination Plant operation.

## Why Do These Plants Need Strong Corrosion Protection?
Seawater is loaded with chloride, which eats through untreated metal pipes, tanks, and valves far faster than plain freshwater. That is why every World’s Largest Desalination Plant facility leans on protective coatings for the equipment that keeps it running.
Skip that protection and corrosion catches up fast, bringing leaks, sudden shutdowns, and repair bills nobody budgeted for. Fusion Bonded Epoxy coating, better known as FBE, exists to head off that failure before it starts.

## How Does FBE Coating Support Desalination Plant Infrastructure?
Inside the world’s largest desalination plant system, FBE coating stands between bare steel and a chloride-heavy environment that would otherwise eat it alive. Once applied, it bonds tightly to the metal and forms a barrier that chemicals and moisture struggle to cross.
**Reasons plants keep choosing FBE for the world’s largest desalination plant project:**
*   Strong corrosion protection in chloride-rich environments  
*   High adhesion, so the coating does not lift or peel  
*   Resistance to water treatment chemicals  
*   Tough enough to handle sand and suspended solids  
*   A smoother internal surface for better water flow  
*   A working life of 25 to 40 years, when maintained properly  
*   Fewer repairs across that lifespan  
*   Approval for potable water systems, where applicable

Freshwater demand is not going to level off soon, so the World’s Largest Desalination Plant sector will keep growing with it. New projects are already taking shape across the Middle East, India, and beyond.
Where this industry ends up depends on smarter technology, tougher corrosion-resistant materials, and engineers who get the details right the first time. FBE coating will keep playing a part, since a coating failure in a chloride-heavy plant is never cheap.

# Desalination
### What makes water saline?
What do we mean by "saline water?" Water that is saline contains significant amounts (referred to as "concentrations") of dissolved salts. In this case, the concentration is the amount (by weight) of salt in water, as expressed in "parts per million" (ppm). If water has a concentration of 10,000 ppm of dissolved salts, then one percent of the weight of the water comes from dissolved salts.
Here are our parameters for saline water:
*   Fresh water - Less than 1,000 ppm  
*   Slightly saline water - From 1,000 ppm to 3,000 ppm  
*   Moderately saline water - From 3,000 ppm to 10,000 ppm  
*   Highly saline water - From 10,000 ppm to 35,000 ppm
For context, ocean water contains about 35,000 ppm of salt.

# Desalination
### The worldwide need for freshwater
The scarcity of fresh water resources and the need for additional water supplies is already critical in many arid regions of the world and will be increasingly important in the future. Many arid areas simply do not have fresh water resources in the form of surface water such as rivers and lakes. They may have only limited **underground water resources****(****groundwater****)**, some that are becoming more brackish as extraction of water from the aquifers continues. Solar desalination - evaporation - is used by nature to produce **rain**, which is the main source of fresh water on earth.
According to the International Desalination Association, globally, more than 300 million people receive their water from de-salination plants. The largest desalination plant in North America, the Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant, can be found near San Diego, California. It produces 50 million gallons a day of fresh water for 110,000 customers in San Diego County where approximately 3.3 million people live.It costs about twice as much as other water sources. At this moment there exists 11 desalination plants in California and 10 more plants have been proposed. The largest desalination plant in the world, Jebel Ali Power Plant and Water Desalination, is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and produces over 588 million gallons of potable water a day.
In 2015, in some States in the U.S., public supply water sources include desalinated seawater or brackish groundwater that has been treated to reduce dissolved solids. A combined total of 7.21 million gallons per day of saline surface water withdrawals for public supply use were reported for the U.S. Virgin Islands, Texas, Florida, and Massachusetts. A combined total of 263 million gallons per day of saline groundwater withdrawals for public-supply use were identified for Florida, California, Texas, Virginia, Kansas, and Utah. (Deiter et al., 2018).

# Desalination
### Another method: Reverse osmosis
Another way saline water is desalinized is by the "reverse osmosis" procedure. In most simplistic terms, water, containing dissolved salt molecules, is forced through a semi-permeable membrane (essentially a filter), in which the larger salt molecules do not get through the membrane holes but the smaller water molecules do.
Reverse osmosis is an effective means to desalinate saline water, but it is more expensive than other methods. As prices come down in the future the use of reverse osmosis plants to desalinate large amounts of saline water should become more common.

# Desalination
### Desalination is not modern science
Distillation desalination is one of mankind's earliest forms of water treatment, and it is still a popular treatment solution throughout the world today. In ancient times, many civilizations used this process on their ships to convert sea water into drinking water. Today, desalination plants are used to convert sea water to drinking water on ships and in many arid regions of the world, and to treat water in other areas that is fouled by natural and unnatural contaminants. Distillation is perhaps the one water treatment technology that most completely reduces the widest range of drinking water contaminants.
In nature, this basic process is responsible for the**water (hydrologic) cycle**. The sun supplies energy that causes water to evaporate from surface sources such as lakes, oceans, and streams. The **water vapor** eventually comes in contact with cooler air, where it re-condenses to form dew or rain. This process can be imitated artificially and more rapidly than in nature, using alternative sources of heating and cooling.

# Desalination
### Why don't we see more desalination plants if freshwater is so scarce?
The primary reason we don't see more desalination plants is due to the cost to operate these plants. Salt dissolves easily in water and it requires a lot of energy to break the chemical bonds. Energy consumption hikes up the cost to run a plant and the cost of the technology to desalinate the water also holds a hefty price tag.
Sometimes environmental protection is a factor that can keep desalination plants from being built. In 2022, after a 20-year plan to build a desalination plant at Huntington Beach in California, the California Coastal Commission declined the bid to build the plant due to concerns about higher water rates, marine life loss, and impacts to poor households already living near industrial areas. Residents in the area did not like that the plant would have taken 100 million daily gallons of seawater, desalted half of it, and discharged the other half back as saltier brine.

Many arid areas simply do not have fresh water resources in the form of surface water such as rivers and lakes. They may have only limited **underground water resources****(****groundwater****)**, some that are becoming more brackish as extraction of water from the aquifers continues. Solar desalination - evaporation - is used by nature to produce **rain**, which is the main source of fresh water on earth.
According to the International Desalination Association, globally, more than 300 million people receive their water from de-salination plants. The largest desalination plant in North America, the Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant, can be found near San Diego, California. It produces 50 million gallons a day of fresh water for 110,000 customers in San Diego County where approximately 3.3 million people live.It costs about twice as much as other water sources. At this moment there exists 11 desalination plants in California and 10 more plants have been proposed. The largest desalination plant in the world, Jebel Ali Power Plant and Water Desalination, is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and produces over 588 million gallons of potable water a day.
In 2015, in some States in the U.S., public supply water sources include desalinated seawater or brackish groundwater that has been treated to reduce dissolved solids. A combined total of 7.21 million gallons per day of saline surface water withdrawals for public supply use were reported for the U.S. Virgin Islands, Texas, Florida, and Massachusetts. A combined total of 263 million gallons per day of saline groundwater withdrawals for public-supply use were identified for Florida, California, Texas, Virginia, Kansas, and Utah. (Deiter et al., 2018).

# Desalination
### Another method: Reverse osmosis
Another way saline water is desalinized is by the "reverse osmosis" procedure. In most simplistic terms, water, containing dissolved salt molecules, is forced through a semi-permeable membrane (essentially a filter), in which the larger salt molecules do not get through the membrane holes but the smaller water molecules do.
Reverse osmosis is an effective means to desalinate saline water, but it is more expensive than other methods. As prices come down in the future the use of reverse osmosis plants to desalinate large amounts of saline water should become more common.

# Desalination
### Uses for desalinated water
When we think of desalination we tend to focus on having fresh water to drink but it is important to note that desalinated seawater is not only produced for domestic/municipal use. Desalination provides fresh water for agricultural irrigation and is often used for processes that require extremely good water quality like that used in boilers to avoid scale buildup. Other examples include the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, semi-conductors, and hard disk drives.

# Desalination
### Desalination is not modern science
Distillation desalination is one of mankind's earliest forms of water treatment, and it is still a popular treatment solution throughout the world today. In ancient times, many civilizations used this process on their ships to convert sea water into drinking water. Today, desalination plants are used to convert sea water to drinking water on ships and in many arid regions of the world, and to treat water in other areas that is fouled by natural and unnatural contaminants. Distillation is perhaps the one water treatment technology that most completely reduces the widest range of drinking water contaminants.
In nature, this basic process is responsible for the**water (hydrologic) cycle**. The sun supplies energy that causes water to evaporate from surface sources such as lakes, oceans, and streams. The **water vapor** eventually comes in contact with cooler air, where it re-condenses to form dew or rain. This process can be imitated artificially and more rapidly than in nature, using alternative sources of heating and cooling.

# Desalination
### What makes water saline?
What do we mean by "saline water?" Water that is saline contains significant amounts (referred to as "concentrations") of dissolved salts. In this case, the concentration is the amount (by weight) of salt in water, as expressed in "parts per million" (ppm). If water has a concentration of 10,000 ppm of dissolved salts, then one percent of the weight of the water comes from dissolved salts.
Here are our parameters for saline water:
*   Fresh water - Less than 1,000 ppm  
*   Slightly saline water - From 1,000 ppm to 3,000 ppm  
*   Moderately saline water - From 3,000 ppm to 10,000 ppm  
*   Highly saline water - From 10,000 ppm to 35,000 ppm
For context, ocean water contains about 35,000 ppm of salt.

### Why don't we see more desalination plants if freshwater is so scarce?
The primary reason we don't see more desalination plants is due to the cost to operate these plants. Salt dissolves easily in water and it requires a lot of energy to break the chemical bonds. Energy consumption hikes up the cost to run a plant and the cost of the technology to desalinate the water also holds a hefty price tag.
Sometimes environmental protection is a factor that can keep desalination plants from being built. Ras Al Khair in Saudi Arabia currently holds the World’s Largest Desalination Plant title, producing close to three million cubic meters of fresh water daily. Riyadh and several nearby cities draw drinking water directly from this one site.
Freshwater shortage sits near the top of the world’s problems right now. Growing populations, expanding industries, and shrinking natural water sources have pushed one country after another toward seawater desalination.
A desalination plant strips salt, minerals, and other impurities out of seawater until it is safe to drink, farm with, or run through a factory. The World’s Largest Desalination Plant rankings show how far this technology has come.

## Which Countries Operate the World’s Largest Desalination Plant Facilities?
Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and India host most of the sites on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list. Each country deals with the same problem: limited freshwater and dense coastal populations.
**A few names show up again and again on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant ranking:**
*   Ras Al Khair and Shuaiba, both in Saudi Arabia  
*   Jebel Ali and Taweelah, in the United Arab Emirates  
*   Sorek, in Israel  
*   Nemmeli, in India
None of these sites operates in isolation. Water from each one feeds straight into municipal supply lines, refineries, power plants, and farmland across the region.

## How Do These Facilities Turn Seawater Into Freshwater?
Reverse Osmosis is the workhorse behind most facilities on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list, though Multi-Stage Flash and Multi-Effect Distillation still show up at several sites. It forces seawater through fine membranes that trap salt and other particles, letting only clean water pass through.
Thermal plants heat seawater until it evaporates, then collect the vapor as pure water. Quite a few large sites run both methods side by side.
Around 300 million people worldwide now rely, one way or another, on water from a World’s Largest Desalination Plant operation.

## Why Do These Plants Need Strong Corrosion Protection?
Seawater is loaded with chloride, which eats through untreated metal pipes, tanks, and valves far faster than plain freshwater. That is why every World’s Largest Desalination Plant facility leans on protective coatings for the equipment that keeps it running.
Skip that protection and corrosion catches up fast, bringing leaks, sudden shutdowns, and repair bills nobody budgeted for. Fusion Bonded Epoxy coating, better known as FBE, exists to head off that failure before it starts.

The **Ras Al-Khair Power and Desalination Plant** is a power and desalination plant located in Ras Al-Khair on the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia. It is operated by the Saline Water Conversion Corporation of Saudi Arabia. The plant began operating in April 2014 and, as of January 2017, is the world's largest hybrid water desalination plant.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-2) The project includes a power plant capable of producing 2400 MW of electricity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1) In 2015, it won the Global Water Awards "Desalination Plant of the Year" award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-4)
Construction of the plant began in 2011.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Though originally slated to begin producing freshwater by the end of 2013,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-6) the first freshwater produced from the plant was in early 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett2-7) Full commercial operation of the plant was achieved in March 2016.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-8)

The primary contractors for construction of the plant were the Doosan Group and Saudi Archirodon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Doosan was awarded the prime contract in September, 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett1-9) Additional contractors for the plant included Fluid Equipment Development Company for energy recovery devices, Siemens for generators, turbines, and related equipment, and Hyosung for various motors.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)
The plant has created 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-10)

Water intake for the plant comes from the Persian Gulf, on the shore of which the plant sits.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) The plant includes five high-efficiency gas turbines operated in combined cycle mode and in single mode.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) It uses a hybrid system of eight multi-stage flashing units and 17 reverse osmosis units.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-11) Freshwater output from the plant is pumped via pipelines to Riyadh and Hafr Al-Batin.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1) Electricity and freshwater output from the plant also supply a nearby aluminium oxide refinery.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Of the 2400 MW electricity produced by the plant, 200 MW are used by the plant itself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett2-7)Effluent from the plant is processed locally by a dedicated wastewater treatment plant and discharged into the Persian Gulf.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)

Ras Al Khair in Saudi Arabia currently holds the World’s Largest Desalination Plant title, producing close to three million cubic meters of fresh water daily. Riyadh and several nearby cities draw drinking water directly from this one site.
Freshwater shortage sits near the top of the world’s problems right now. Growing populations, expanding industries, and shrinking natural water sources have pushed one country after another toward seawater desalination.
A desalination plant strips salt, minerals, and other impurities out of seawater until it is safe to drink, farm with, or run through a factory. The World’s Largest Desalination Plant rankings show how far this technology has come.

## Which Countries Operate the World’s Largest Desalination Plant Facilities?
Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and India host most of the sites on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list. Each country deals with the same problem: limited freshwater and dense coastal populations.
**A few names show up again and again on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant ranking:**
*   Ras Al Khair and Shuaiba, both in Saudi Arabia  
*   Jebel Ali and Taweelah, in the United Arab Emirates  
*   Sorek, in Israel  
*   Nemmeli, in India
None of these sites operates in isolation. Water from each one feeds straight into municipal supply lines, refineries, power plants, and farmland across the region.

## How Do These Facilities Turn Seawater Into Freshwater?
Reverse Osmosis is the workhorse behind most facilities on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list, though Multi-Stage Flash and Multi-Effect Distillation still show up at several sites. It forces seawater through fine membranes that trap salt and other particles, letting only clean water pass through.
Thermal plants heat seawater until it evaporates, then collect the vapor as pure water. Quite a few large sites run both methods side by side.
Around 300 million people worldwide now rely, one way or another, on water from a World’s Largest Desalination Plant operation.

## Why Do These Plants Need Strong Corrosion Protection?
Seawater is loaded with chloride, which eats through untreated metal pipes, tanks, and valves far faster than plain freshwater. That is why every World’s Largest Desalination Plant facility leans on protective coatings for the equipment that keeps it running.
Skip that protection and corrosion catches up fast, bringing leaks, sudden shutdowns, and repair bills nobody budgeted for. Fusion Bonded Epoxy coating, better known as FBE, exists to head off that failure before it starts.

## How Does FBE Coating Support Desalination Plant Infrastructure?
Inside the world’s largest desalination plant system, FBE coating stands between bare steel and a chloride-heavy environment that would otherwise eat it alive. Once applied, it bonds tightly to the metal and forms a barrier that chemicals and moisture struggle to cross.
**Reasons plants keep choosing FBE for the world’s largest desalination plant project:**
*   Strong corrosion protection in chloride-rich environments  
*   High adhesion, so the coating does not lift or peel  
*   Resistance to water treatment chemicals  
*   Tough enough to handle sand and suspended solids  
*   A smoother internal surface for better water flow  
*   A working life of 25 to 40 years, when maintained properly  
*   Fewer repairs across that lifespan  
*   Approval for potable water systems, where applicable

Freshwater demand is not going to level off soon, so the World’s Largest Desalination Plant sector will keep growing with it. New projects are already taking shape across the Middle East, India, and beyond.

The **Ras Al-Khair Power and Desalination Plant** is a power and desalination plant located in Ras Al-Khair on the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia. It is operated by the Saline Water Conversion Corporation of Saudi Arabia. The plant began operating in April 2014 and, as of January 2017, is the world's largest hybrid water desalination plant.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-2) The project includes a power plant capable of producing 2400 MW of electricity.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1) In 2015, it won the Global Water Awards "Desalination Plant of the Year" award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-4)
Construction of the plant began in 2011.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Though originally slated to begin producing freshwater by the end of 2013,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-6) the first freshwater produced from the plant was in early 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett2-7) Full commercial operation of the plant was achieved in March 2016.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-8)
texts.2:
The primary contractors for construction of the plant were the Doosan Group and Saudi Archirodon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Doosan was awarded the prime contract in September, 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett1-9) Additional contractors for the plant included Fluid Equipment Development Company for energy recovery devices, Siemens for generators, turbines, and related equipment, and Hyosung for various motors.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)
The plant has created 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-10)
texts.3:
Water intake for the plant comes from the Persian Gulf, on the shore of which the plant sits.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) The plant includes five high-efficiency gas turbines operated in combined cycle mode and in single mode.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) It uses a hybrid system of eight multi-stage flashing units and 17 reverse osmosis units.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-11) Freshwater output from the plant is pumped via pipelines to Riyadh and Hafr Al-Batin.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1) Electricity and freshwater output from the plant also supply a nearby aluminium oxide refinery.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Of the 2400 MW electricity produced by the plant, 200 MW are used by the plant itself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett2-7)Effluent from the plant is processed locally by a dedicated wastewater treatment plant and discharged into the Persian Gulf.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)

Ras Al Khair in Saudi Arabia currently holds the World’s Largest Desalination Plant title, producing close to three million cubic meters of fresh water daily. Riyadh and several nearby cities draw drinking water directly from this one site.
Freshwater shortage sits near the top of the world’s problems right now. Growing populations, expanding industries, and shrinking natural water sources have pushed one country after another toward seawater desalination.
A desalination plant strips salt, minerals, and other impurities out of seawater until it is safe to drink, farm with, or run through a factory. The World’s Largest Desalination Plant rankings show how far this technology has come.

## Which Countries Operate the World’s Largest Desalination Plant Facilities?
Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and India host most of the sites on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list. Each country deals with the same problem: limited freshwater and dense coastal populations.
**A few names show up again and again on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant ranking:**
*   Ras Al Khair and Shuaiba, both in Saudi Arabia  
*   Jebel Ali and Taweelah, in the United Arab Emirates  
*   Sorek, in Israel  
*   Nemmeli, in India
None of these sites operates in isolation. Water from each one feeds straight into municipal supply lines, refineries, power plants, and farmland across the region.

## How Do These Facilities Turn Seawater Into Freshwater?
Reverse Osmosis is the workhorse behind most facilities on the World’s Largest Desalination Plant list, though Multi-Stage Flash and Multi-Effect Distillation still show up at several sites. It forces seawater through fine membranes that trap salt and other particles, letting only clean water pass through.
Thermal plants heat seawater until it evaporates, then collect the vapor as pure water. Quite a few large sites run both methods side by side.
Around 300 million people worldwide now rely, one way or another, on water from a World’s Largest Desalination Plant operation.

## Why Do These Plants Need Strong Corrosion Protection?
Seawater is loaded with chloride, which eats through untreated metal pipes, tanks, and valves far faster than plain freshwater. That is why every World’s Largest Desalination Plant facility leans on protective coatings for the equipment that keeps it running.
Skip that protection and corrosion catches up fast, bringing leaks, sudden shutdowns, and repair bills nobody budgeted for. Fusion Bonded Epoxy coating, better known as FBE, exists to head off that failure before it starts.

## How Does FBE Coating Support Desalination Plant Infrastructure?
Inside the world’s largest desalination plant system, FBE coating stands between bare steel and a chloride-heavy environment that would otherwise eat it alive. Once applied, it bonds tightly to the metal and forms a barrier that chemicals and moisture struggle to cross.
**Reasons plants keep choosing FBE for the world’s largest desalination plant project:**
*   Strong corrosion protection in chloride-rich environments  
*   High adhesion, so the coating does not lift or peel  
*   Resistance to water treatment chemicals  
*   Tough enough to handle sand and suspended solids  
*   A smoother internal surface for better water flow  
*   A working life of 25 to 40 years, when maintained properly  
*   Fewer repairs across that lifespan  
*   Approval for potable water systems, where applicable

Freshwater demand is not going to level off soon, so the World’s Largest Desalination Plant sector will keep growing with it. New projects are already taking shape across the Middle East, India, and beyond.

The primary contractors for construction of the plant were the Doosan Group and Saudi Archirodon.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Doosan was awarded the prime contract in September, 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett1-9) Additional contractors for the plant included Fluid Equipment Development Company for energy recovery devices, Siemens for generators, turbines, and related equipment, and Hyosung for various motors.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)
The plant has created 3,500 direct and indirect jobs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-10)

Water intake for the plant comes from the Persian Gulf, on the shore of which the plant sits.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) The plant includes five high-efficiency gas turbines operated in combined cycle mode and in single mode.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) It uses a hybrid system of eight multi-stage flashing units and 17 reverse osmosis units.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-11) Freshwater output from the plant is pumped via pipelines to Riyadh and Hafr Al-Batin.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-StartsPumping-1) Electricity and freshwater output from the plant also supply a nearby aluminium oxide refinery.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5) Of the 2400 MW electricity produced by the plant, 200 MW are used by the plant itself.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-Bennett2-7)Effluent from the plant is processed locally by a dedicated wastewater treatment plant and discharged into the Persian Gulf.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ras_Al-Khair_Power_and_Desalination_Plant#cite_note-WaterTechnology-5)
